# Plumfield Library

> Plumfield Living Books Library is a private lending library in Denmark, Wisconsin, serving families, educators, and lifelong learners with about 12,000 carefully curated titles centered on truth, goodness, and beauty. We offer book clubs, classes, workshops, and enrichment opportunities, with a branch in Pulaski.

The library grew out of the work surrounding Plumfield Moms and a broader commitment to classical education, living books, and the preservation of literary heritage. Rather than focusing primarily on newly published titles, the collection emphasizes books that have demonstrated lasting worth through decades of readership. Many of these works are out of print, overlooked by modern publishing trends, or unavailable through local libraries.

Plumfield Library exists to remove barriers between readers and these books. By acquiring, cataloging, and lending carefully selected titles, the library provides families, students, homeschoolers, and schools with access to works that might otherwise remain inaccessible. The collection spans literature, history, biography, science, theology, children’s books, and educational resources, with particular attention given to books that cultivate knowledge, imagination, virtue, and a deeper understanding of the human experience.

The library is operated with a stewardship mindset. Resources are directed toward preserving access, maintaining accurate catalog records, and creating practical systems that allow a relatively small organization to serve a growing community. Technology is used to support the mission, not replace it: cataloging, discovery, circulation, and digital tools are developed to make meaningful books easier to find and borrow.

At its heart, Plumfield Library is an effort to preserve and share a body of literature that might otherwise fade from public awareness. Its purpose is not merely to store books, but to connect readers with works that have shaped minds, inspired curiosity, and enriched lives across generations.

The Library is owned and operated by the Masarik Family:

**Sara** is the head librarian and the founder of Plumfield. Her children, **Michael**, **Greta**, and **Jack** all serve various roles in the operation of the library.
- **Michael** handles all IT relating to the Library
- **Greta** runs point on circulation and book recomendation
- **Jack** recomends books to patrons and is the graphic designer for the library and for our press ([Plumfield Press](https://plumfieldpress.com))

## Library Classes

### Policy overview

Plumfield Library classes are available to members through the Patron Dashboard. This policy explains registration, payments, and cancellation rules.

### Key points

- Full Membership gives access to class registration in the Patron Dashboard.
- Invoices can be viewed and paid through the dashboard.
- Classes are non-refundable; if a class is canceled by the teacher, Plumfield will work toward a fair solution.

Read the full human page at [/library-policies/classes](/library-policies/classes).

---

## Patron Dashboard

### Policy overview

The Patron Dashboard is the central hub for managing membership, classes, invoices, branch information, and interlibrary loan requests.

### Key points

- Use the dashboard to view invoices, class registrations, and branch details.
- Sign in with your email to receive a one-time login link.
- The dashboard also provides access to interlibrary loan request forms and class sign-ups.

Read the full human page at [/library-policies/dashboard](/library-policies/dashboard).

---

## Holds

### Policy overview

Holds can only be placed from the Plumfield Library Libib catalog. This policy explains why holds are not available through the patron dashboard and how to place them.

### Key points

- Holds must be placed from the Libib website.
- Requests must be submitted at least 48 hours before pickup.
- For holds to be picked up at other branches, refer to the Interlibrary Loan policy.

Read the full human page at [/library-policies/holds](/library-policies/holds).

---

## Interlibrary Loan

### Policy overview

Plumfield Library is building an interlibrary loan process to connect patrons with books from the Main Library. This policy describes how to request an interlibrary loan and what to expect.

### Key points

- Place holds normally through Libib.
- Use the patron dashboard to submit one request form per book.
- The book is checked out when it ships and may take up to two weeks.
- Interlibrary loans are checked out for 60 days and may not be renewed.

Read the full human page at [/library-policies/interlibrary-loan](/library-policies/interlibrary-loan).

---

## Main Library Rules

### Policy overview

The Main Library is designed to be welcoming, safe, and peaceful for families and children. These rules help preserve the shared space, protect people and pets, and support the calm, gentle rhythm of Plumfield Library.

### Key points

- Indoor play is welcome, but no shouting, rough-housing, wrestling, throwing, or hide-and-seek inside the house.
- Please do not play on stairs or railings, and children should only be upstairs when a library volunteer or teacher is present.
- The bedrooms and many basement areas are always off limits; the living and dining rooms are available only during club days with adult supervision.
- Enjoy quiet activities on the couches, such as knitting, crocheting, reading, or visiting, but avoid romping or pillow fights.
- The front yard is open for guests, while the side yard, back yard, camper area, and garage are not part of the library.
- Park in the cul-de-sac, not in the driveway, for the safety of small children and dogs.
- The dogs are friendly, but please let them be, avoid offering toys or food, and do not wrestle or throw things for them.

Read the full human page at [/library-policies/main-rules](/library-policies/main-rules).

---

## Parent-Present Policy

### Policy overview

Plumfield Living Library requires parents, guardians, or responsible adults to remain present and available during any library class, gathering, or visit unless otherwise stated in writing.

### Key points

- Parents or responsible adults must stay on site for the full duration of Plumfield activities.
- This policy applies at all locations, including outdoor areas and branch spaces.
- Children age 5 and under need close support throughout activities.
- Plumfield may ask families to step out or withdraw if a child’s needs become unsafe or disruptive.

Read the full human page at [/library-policies/parent-present](/library-policies/parent-present).

---

## Renewals

### Policy overview

Plumfield Library does not offer renewals at this time. With so many readers enjoying our books, keeping them circulating is one of the most important ways we steward what we have. The 45-day loan period gives each family a generous window with their books, and returning them on time means the next family gets their turn.

### Key points

- Renewals are not offered while the library maintains fair circulation for all families.
- Patrons may return a book and check it out again if no one else is waiting for it.
- The library's software and multi-location tracking make managed renewals impractical for the small team.
- New mothers may keep books for up to three months during maternity leave with prior arrangement.

Read the full human page at [/library-policies/renewals](/library-policies/renewals).

---

## Shire Branch Rules

### Policy overview

Shire Branch offers a warm, family-focused library experience with specific boundaries to keep children safe and to protect the home and grounds. These rules make it possible to enjoy both indoor play and outdoor space while respecting private areas, farm equipment, and animals.

### Key points

- Indoor play is encouraged in the basement children’s area, but no shouting, rough-housing, wrestling, throwing, or hide-and-seek anywhere in the house.
- The basement bathroom and living room are open for use, but the basement kitchen, root cellar, back furnace room, and office are not part of the library.
- Please do not play on stairs or railings; the bedrooms, all closets, and the second floor are not part of the library.
- Quiet, seated activities are welcome on the couches, but no romping or pillow-fighting at any time.
- Park on the grass along the driveway or by the shop garage, leaving the main garage area clear for safety.
- Do not enter any outbuilding, including the shop, shop garage, or tractor shed, because dangerous tools and farm equipment are stored there.
- Outdoor play is welcome within the mowed grass areas, and the gardens may be enjoyed from the pathways only.
- The trampoline, swing set, and outdoor playthings are available under parental supervision, with a limit of six children on the trampoline at once.
- Hunter the cat may be petted gently, but please do not tease him or try to play with him, as he may nip.
- Please watch the chickens from a distance and do not enter their coop or fenced area; avoid picking up eggs you find in the yard.

Read the full human page at [/library-policies/shire-rules](/library-policies/shire-rules).

---

## Volunteers

### Policy overview

Plumfield Library is temporarily pausing new volunteer and internship applications as the library grows, launches new programs, and brings more than 30 books back into print. This pause helps the team train and welcome volunteers well rather than in the midst of transition.

### Key points

- New volunteer applications and internships are currently on hold.
- The pause allows the team to focus on growth and stable operations.
- Plumfield is prayerfully discerning the best way to train and support volunteers before relaunching the program.

Read the full human page at [/library-policies/volunteers](/library-policies/volunteers).
